_description: Coarticulation rules for connected speech. Locus equations from Sussman et al. (1991), resistance values from articulatory constraint studies.

locus_equations._description: F2 onset = slope * F2_vowel + intercept (Hz). From Sussman et al. 1991.

resistance._description: Per-articulator resistance to coarticulation (0=fully coarticulated, 1=fixed). Higher values mean the articulator resists neighboring phone influence.

stop._note: Stops require precise closure — most articulators resist coarticulation

fricative._note: Fricatives need narrow constriction but allow some coarticulation

nasal._note: Velum must stay open; oral closure point resists but jaw can vary

vowel._note: Vowels are most susceptible to coarticulation — open tract allows blending

approximant._note: Moderate resistance — slight constriction allows some blending

lateral._note: Tongue tip must stay for central closure, but body can coarticulate

tap._note: Very brief — almost fully coarticulated with neighbors

transition_multipliers._description: Multiplier on base transition duration by manner of the target phone. Smaller = faster transition.

anticipatory_lookahead._description: How far ahead (in phones) each articulator anticipates
anticipatory_lookahead._note: Lip rounding anticipates furthest ahead (3 phones in 'stew'), velum opens/closes early
